minutes.headline: Open Space Committee took no action on a 20 Kilburn right-of-first-refusal issue, tabling it to the next meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee approved March minutes, discussed membership changes (new at-large member, new planning board rep), and agreed to hold a joint meeting with the planning board for rights of first refusal. Most of the meeting concerned the 20 Kilburn parcel, where no formal right of first refusal was received; members will review the Select Board meeting and follow up with the town manager. Members also began discussing updating the open space plan acquisition guidelines and heard about the MBTA Communities Act.

what_happened.line: The committee tabled the 20 Kilburn matter to its next meeting after no formal right of first refusal was reported received.
Two members will review the Select Board record on 20 Kilburn and follow up with the town manager.
The committee agreed to attend the planning board's meeting for a joint session whenever rights of first refusal arise.
An agenda item will be added to discuss amending the six acquisition criteria, followed by public input on the open space plan update.
The next meeting is set for August 14th, and members discussed possibly moving the September 11th meeting.

why_it_matters: A town right of first refusal on a parcel under Chapter 61 comes with a short window to act, so a tabled item and an unsettled process bear on whether land at 20 Kilburn could be considered for open space.
The planned review of the acquisition criteria and the plan update affect which land the town may pursue, and a valid open space plan is needed for some state recreation and conservation grants.
